title: Tesla's Two-Pronged Move: FSD Ad Placed in New York's Times Square, Grok Bot Dazzles and Lights Up Las Vegas Sphere
excerpt: In traditional marketing thinking, Tesla has long been known for "zero traditional advertising," relying mainly on brand reputation and fan-driven viral growth
content_html:
In traditional marketing thinking, Tesla has long been known for "zero traditional advertising," relying mainly on brand reputation and fan-driven viral growth for promotion. However, this strategy is undergoing a subtle shift. Recently, Tesla and its related businesses simultaneously launched high-profile campaigns at two major North American landmarks, showcasing their latest advances in intelligent driving and artificial intelligence.

New York's Times Square Welcomes First FSD Ad, With Core Data Fully Disclosed

As one of the world's busiest commercial hubs, New York's Times Square has welcomed a highly anticipated Tesla FSD (Supervised) ad. The promotional video appears on the large curved billboard of Chase bank there and will continue to run on a loop for the remainder of November.

The ad focuses on FSD's performance in real-world complex driving scenarios and presents two key data points: first, "when engaged, it is 7 times safer than a human driver"; second, "over 15 billion miles (about 24.14 billion kilometers) driven cumulatively worldwide." In addition, the Chase logo appears multiple times in the ad to promote the two companies' close cooperation in auto financing.

Looking back at Tesla's history, it did not begin gradually experimenting with paid advertising until 2023. Unlike before, the core of Tesla's heavy investment in this promotion is not the vehicle hardware itself, but its underlying software service capabilities.

Recent data shows that the number of FSD subscribers reached a record high of 1.74 million in the third quarter of this year, and as many as 75% of new vehicle orders in North America selected the feature. To further expand subscriptions, Elon Musk previously decided to remove basic Autopilot from new vehicle orders, pushing more owners toward FSD. Tesla has also continued to encourage word-of-mouth promotion through the launch of an FSD referral program. In international markets, the feature is also accelerating its rollout: Finland has just become the 11th EU country to approve it, and the EU is expected to hold a formal vote in December on approval across the entire European Union.

Grok Bot Also Shines on Las Vegas Sphere, Making a Full Push into Vehicles and Enterprise Services

In addition to the FSD campaign in Times Square, Musk's AI business also enjoyed a highlight moment in Las Vegas.

On the famous local landmark, the Las Vegas Sphere, SpaceXSI ran a visually striking giant ad for Grok Bot. The entire giant sphere was wrapped as a blue Grok Bot racing helmet, with the Las Vegas Grand Prix track clearly displayed below. At the end, the ad showcased a large number of brightly colored Grok Bot characters, visually presenting its intelligent application capabilities in fields such as sales and customer support.

It is worth noting that Tesla has now officially brought Grok Bot into its in-car system. Drivers can use this AI agent to handle various daily matters and complex tasks while driving through voice or seamless interaction. As the EU's approval process for FSD enters its final sprint, Tesla is expected to launch comprehensive brand and technology promotion in more core global markets in the future.
